brief.title: 2026-10-19 AI 简报：MCP 权限注入、Harness 增益归因与终端 Agent
brief.overview: 本期可见内容为 5 篇 arXiv 公告论文（announced_at 均为 2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00）。其中 4 篇首次提交于 2026-10-15，da92b80397690dde35e8 首次提交于 2026-07-27；并非 5 篇均在 2026-10-15 首次提交。

items.title: Structured Authority Injection: Persistent Human Control for LLM Agents via Typed MCP Overrides
items.summary: 论文提出 Structured Authority Injection（SAI）协议：把操作者的纠正改写为经 schema 校验的 MCP 类型化工具调用，并维护按优先级排序的“权威上下文”加在每次 LLM prompt 之前，使纠正经规划过程不可访问的定向通道执行。方法无需微调、无需模型权重，适用于支持 MCP 工具调用的指令微调模型。在 9 个 LLM、8 类针对 Agent 失效模式的场景中，论文称歧义指令解释减少、多轮规划中的“权威衰减”得到缓解，最强模型的 prompt 开销最多降低 38%（该比例随模型与场景变化），并明确说明收益跨模型差异很大。
items.why_it_matters: 你的关键词是工具调用：如果后端 Agent 依赖 MCP，这套“提高优先级的结构化工具调用 + 排序权威上下文”思路可直接落到接口设计上，比把人类纠正混进自由文本更可审计，而且不需要重训模型。

items.title: Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution
items.summary: 针对自动优化 Agent harness（prompt、技能、工具、编排代码）的“进化增益”，论文提出 Harness-Delta Attribution（HDA）评估协议，把增益拆为三部分：产物导致的过拟合、测试时扩展可解释的部分、以及残余可泛化改进的上界。在 21 个搜索集增益统计显著的设置中，过拟合与测试时扩展平均分别解释 54% 和 14% 的增益，两者合计在 14 个设置中超过 50%；搜索集上的增益常无法迁移到留出任务，且论文指出仅靠验证集信号不足以阻止过拟合。
items.why_it_matters: 如果你在用自动搜索优化 Agent 的 prompt/工具链，这篇给出了一套“涨点归因”检查法：先扣掉过拟合和测试时扩展，再看还剩多少可迁移改进，可避免把搜索集收益当成产品收益。

items.title: Lean4AgenticRL: Advancing Agentic RL with Verifiable Multi-level Process Rewards
items.summary: Lean4AgenticRL 将开放式 agentic RL 的多层过程奖励统一建立在 Lean4 形式化 schema 上：先为问题构建专用 workflow，再把 workflow 形式化、在通用 harness 中做多级奖励标注，并用 workflow-stage-normalized GRPO 训练。作者称这是首个把多层过程奖励落到统一 Lean4 形式化的框架。LAR-27B 在 TerminalBench-2.1 上达到 77.3%；作者的 LAR-9B/27B 模型平均比基础模型高 9.89%、比作者所知的同规模第二好模型高 5.07%（原文以百分比表述，未给出分母细节）。
items.why_it_matters: 对应“AI 编程”方向：TerminalBench 是终端/编码 Agent 的常用基准，77.3% 与相对提升幅度可作为你评估自建编码 Agent 或选择开源后训练模型的参照，但注意这是特定基准上的成绩，不是通用能力结论。

items.title: PRIME: Towards Verifiable Evidence-Grounded Reasoning in LLM Agents
items.summary: PRIME（Precommitted Rules for Inference from Minimal Evidence）在检查前先固定“证据路径”，规定每条结论可以如何被证成；独立程序记录每次检查结果，拒绝没有证据支持的结论，并可指出能支撑更强结论的检查或直接执行这些检查。在 480 个公开记录任务上，仅看到要求的 Agent 在 26.7% 的任务中给出无依据结论，PRIME 为 0；其指引与追加检查把“有依据结论”的平均分从仅拒答时的 30.1 提升到该指标的上限 59.2（满分 100，即该评分体系能给的最高分）。
items.why_it_matters: 可作 Agent 落地护栏的参考：把“先定证据规则、再让模型下结论”写成显式流程与检查记录，而不是事后校验；代价也很清楚——只拒答只能拿 30.1 分，必须补做检查才能提高有用性。

items.title: Don't Retrain, Remix: Adaptation of Web Agents using Mixture Hypernetworks
items.summary: WebMix 用混合超网络做 Web Agent 的免重训适配：先在一批源界面上训练低秩适配器库；部署时一个 scout agent 探索目标界面并写成紧凑“手册”，轻量 router 根据手册预测混合系数，把已有适配器组合成目标适配器，适配只需一次探索加一次前向，不需要在目标环境做梯度更新。在 TimeWarp 域迁移上，两种模型平均比最佳基线高约 8 个百分点；论文称在 TimeWarp 的域迁移、版本迁移以及 WebArena-Lite-v2 三种设置上均匹配或优于 ICL 与 LoRA 基线。
items.why_it_matters: 对“本地部署”和 Agent 维护有实际意义：新增网站/界面版本时不必重训整个模型，只需适配器组合与前向，适合把模型权重固定在本地、靠轻量适配器扩展能力的部署形态。

{"id": "da92b80397690dde35e8", "title": "Structured Authority Injection: Persistent Human Control for LLM Agents via Typed MCP Overrides", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22373", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-07-27T03:38:01+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-07-27T03:38:01+00:00", "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly used as autonomous orchestrators in distributed and multi-agent systems, yet a control gap remains: no protocol-level mechanism allows human operators to inject binding directives that persist across planning cycles. Free-text overrides suffer from ambiguous interpretation due to lack of schema validation and from authority erosion as operator instructions lose influence within accumulating context. We propose Structured Authority Injection (SAI), a protocol that addresses these issues by routing operator corrections through typed, schema-validated Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool calls and maintaining a ranked authority context prepended to each LLM prompt. SAI defines three override classes (Constraint, Priority, and Strategy) with distinct persistence semantics and an explicit precedence order enforced via a directed authority channel inaccessible to the planning process. The method requires no model fine-tuning or access to model weights and applies to instruction-tuned LLMs supporting MCP tool use. Evaluation across nine LLMs and eight scenarios targeting agent failure modes shows reduced ambiguous directive interpretation and mitigated authority decay across planning iterations, with lower prompt overhead in the strongest models (up to 38% depending on model and scenario), though benefit varies substantially across models. SAI provides a general design pattern for agent systems requiring explicit and persistent human control.", "evidence_kind": "abstract", "demo": false, "publication_kind": "preprint"}

{"id": "f34ad45741b405ff9e69", "title": "Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22466", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-15T17:39:38+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-10-15T17:39:38+00:00", "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "Abstract: Harness evolution automatically optimizes the prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration code around a fixed-weight model, offering a way to improve agentic systems without updating model weights. The agent harness is iteratively optimized to achieve higher performance on the search set. But how much of this gain reflects benchmark-specific overfitting or additional inference-time compute, and how much may generalize beyond the search set? In this work, we introduce Harness-Delta Attribution (HDA), an evaluation protocol that dissects an evolution gain into artifact-driven overfitting, gains explained by test-time scaling, and the remainder, which gives an upper bound on residual generalizable improvement. We apply HDA to 11 executor models and three harness-evolution frameworks across math, coding, creativity, and agentic tasks. In 21 of these settings that show statistically significant search-set gains, we find that a large share of the improvement is explained by overfitting or test-time scaling. Specifically, among these 21 settings, overfitting and test-time scaling account for 54% and 14% of the gain on average; their combined share exceeds 50% in 14 settings. The residual and held-out transfer vary substantially across tasks, models, and frameworks. Importantly, search-set gains often fail to transfer to held-out tasks, and provide limited evidence that they will persist under practical distribution shifts. Moreover, validation-based signals are insufficient to prevent overfitting. These results motivate attribution-aware evaluation in future harness evolution research.", "evidence_kind": "abstract", "demo": false, "publication_kind": "preprint"}

{"id": "a97c1f5a709e4de6f7ba", "title": "Lean4AgenticRL: Advancing Agentic RL with Verifiable Multi-level Process Rewards", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22448", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-15T15:26:54+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-10-15T15:26:54+00:00", "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "Abstract: Enhancing the agentic capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) to tackle complex software engineering (SWE) and general terminal-usage problems is a pressing challenge. Current state-of-the-art LLMs often go through large-scale agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL). However, they mostly rely on high-level outcome rewards, with minimal consideration of low-level toolcall and mid-level workflow-stage rewards, which makes the training less effective. To overcome this limitation, we propose **Lean4AgenticRL**, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first framework that grounds multi-level process rewards in the unified Lean4 formalization schema for open-ended agentic RL. **Lean4AgenticRL** first builds a *problem-specific workflow* system that balances the agent's own capability and controllability during execution, laying the foundation for further verification. Subsequently, our workflow formalization and multi-level reward annotation methods enable agent behavior verification within a general harness system. It provides multi-level rewards to support more effective agentic RL with the workflow-stage-normalized GRPO algorithm. Using **Lean4AgenticRL**, we train **LAR-9B/27B**, a family of models with enhanced agentic capability. Extensive experiments indicate that our model outperforms the leading model of similar size. **LAR-27B** achieves **77.3%** on TerminalBench-2.1. On average, our models outperform the base model by **9.89%** and surpass the second-best model of comparable size we know by **5.07%**. These results indicate the potential of integrating formal methods in enhancing open-ended agentic RL.", "evidence_kind": "abstract", "demo": false, "publication_kind": "preprint"}

{"id": "434246a93fec15537b14", "title": "PRIME: Towards Verifiable Evidence-Grounded Reasoning in LLM Agents", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22426", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-15T05:03:22+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-10-15T05:03:22+00:00", "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "Abstract: LLM agents are used to check records against an organization's requirements, for example whether a vulnerability report is ready for investigation. Requirements often allow several ways to be met, such as a severity rating with a curator-reviewed advisory or a published advisory link. Agents fail by accepting a report after a required check has failed, or by settling for a weaker conclusion without trying another way that could still succeed. We introduce PRIME (Precommitted Rules for Inference from Minimal Evidence). Before checking, it fixes evidence routes specifying how each conclusion may be justified. A separate program records each check result and refuses any conclusion the results do not justify. It also points the agent to checks that could justify a stronger conclusion, or runs them itself. PRIME reports only conclusions authorized by its rules and ledger. With correct requirements, exact checks at known locations, and sufficient budget at stopping, completion reaches the strongest supported conclusion. On 480 public-record tasks, an agent shown the requirements reported unjustified conclusions on 26.7% of tasks, while PRIME reported none. Its directions and added checks raised the average score for justified conclusions from 30.1, with refusal alone, to the maximum of 59.2 out of 100.", "evidence_kind": "abstract", "demo": false, "publication_kind": "preprint"}

{"id": "6ec636eceffcfb5999d5", "title": "Don't Retrain, Remix: Adaptation of Web Agents using Mixture Hypernetworks", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22539", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-15T18:37:41+00:00", "first_published_at": "2026-10-15T18:37:41+00:00", "announced_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "updated_at": null, "feed_entry_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "time_basis": "feed_announcement", "text": "Abstract: The web is not static or uniform. Websites that serve the same purpose can look and navigate very differently. Even within a single site, successive redesigns can change how familiar features are presented and accessed. Humans adapt to this by recognizing familiar interaction patterns and reusing what they already know. We give web agents a similar ability with WebMix, a mixture hypernetwork that adapts them to unseen interfaces by composing previously trained low-rank adapters. WebMix begins with a bank of adapters trained on source interfaces. At deployment, a scout agent explores the target interface and summarizes its observations into a compact manual. A lightweight router uses this manual to predict mixing coefficients over the adapter bank, which combine the existing adapters into a new one for inference. Adapting to a new interface takes only a scouting run and a forward pass, without gradient updates on the target. With Qwen and Llama models, we evaluate domain transfer on TimeWarp and WebArena-Lite-v2, and version transfer on TimeWarp. In all three settings, WebMix matches or outperforms in-context learning and LoRA baselines, often matching the average success of specialists trained directly on those interfaces. On TimeWarp domain transfer, it gains about 8 percentage points on average over the best baseline with both models. These gains do not come at the cost of seen interfaces, where WebMix keeps its lead, and extend to version transfer. Adapting to a new interface can therefore rely on exploration and composition instead of retraining.", "evidence_kind": "abstract", "demo": false, "publication_kind": "preprint"}

arguments.title: 2026-10-19 AI 简报：MCP 权限注入、Harness 增益归因与终端 Agent
arguments.overview: 本期覆盖说明：OpenAI、Google、Hugging Face 三个官方/开源源在过去 24 小时窗口内没有返回条目，TechCrunch 两条均为股权/并购类商业消息（已按“融资”偏好排除）。可用内容来自 arXiv 今日公告列表，以下 5 篇均为 2026 年 10 月 15 日首次提交、今日进入公告的论文，并非今天首次发表。主题集中在工具调用可控性、Agent 评测与部署。
selections: article_id='da92b80397690dde35e8' summary='论文提出 Structured Authority Injection（SAI）协议：把操作者的纠正改写为经 schema 校验的 MCP 类型化工具调用，并维护按优先级排序的“权威上下文”加在每次 LLM prompt 之前，使纠正经规划过程不可访问的定向通道执行。方法无需微调、无需模型权重，适用于支持 MCP 工具调用的指令微调模型。在 9 个 LLM、8 类针对 Agent 失效模式的场景中，论文称歧义指令解释减少、多轮规划中的“权威衰减”得到缓解，最强模型的 prompt 开销最多降低 38%（该比例随模型与场景变化），并明确说明收益跨模型差异很大。' why_it_matters='你的关键词是工具调用：如果后端 Agent 依赖 MCP，这套“提高优先级的结构化工具调用 + 排序权威上下文”思路可直接落到接口设计上，比把人类纠正混进自由文本更可审计，而且不需要重训模型。' topic='Agent / 工具调用' relevance=3

selected_evidence.title: PRIME: Towards Verifiable Evidence-Grounded Reasoning in LLM Agents
selected_evidence.text: Abstract: LLM agents are used to check records against an organization's requirements, for example whether a vulnerability report is ready for investigation. Requirements often allow several ways to be met, such as a severity rating with a curator-reviewed advisory or a published advisory link. Agents fail by accepting a report after a required check has failed, or by settling for a weaker conclusion without trying another way that could still succeed. We introduce PRIME (Precommitted Rules for Inference from Minimal Evidence). Before checking, it fixes evidence routes specifying how each conclusion may be justified. A separate program records each check result and refuses any conclusion the results do not justify. It also points the agent to checks that could justify a stronger conclusion, or runs them itself. PRIME reports only conclusions authorized by its rules and ledger. With correct requirements, exact checks at known locations, and sufficient budget at stopping, completion reaches the strongest supported conclusion. On 480 public-record tasks, an agent shown the requirements reported unjustified conclusions on 26.7% of tasks, while PRIME reported none. Its directions and added checks raised the average score for justified conclusions from 30.1, with refusal alone, to the maximum of 59.2 out of 100.

selected_evidence.title: Don't Retrain, Remix: Adaptation of Web Agents using Mixture Hypernetworks
selected_evidence.text: Abstract: The web is not static or uniform. Websites that serve the same purpose can look and navigate very differently. Even within a single site, successive redesigns can change how familiar features are presented and accessed. Humans adapt to this by recognizing familiar interaction patterns and reusing what they already know. We give web agents a similar ability with WebMix, a mixture hypernetwork that adapts them to unseen interfaces by composing previously trained low-rank adapters. WebMix begins with a bank of adapters trained on source interfaces. At deployment, a scout agent explores the target interface and summarizes its observations into a compact manual. A lightweight router uses this manual to predict mixing coefficients over the adapter bank, which combine the existing adapters into a new one for inference. Adapting to a new interface takes only a scouting run and a forward pass, without gradient updates on the target. With Qwen and Llama models, we evaluate domain transfer on TimeWarp and WebArena-Lite-v2, and version transfer on TimeWarp. In all three settings, WebMix matches or outperforms in-context learning and LoRA baselines, often matching the average success of specialists trained directly on those interfaces. On TimeWarp domain transfer, it gains about 8 percentage points on average over the best baseline with both models. These gains do not come at the cost of seen interfaces, where WebMix keeps its lead, and extend to version transfer. Adapting to a new interface can therefore rely on exploration and composition instead of retraining.

selected_evidence.title: Lean4AgenticRL: Advancing Agentic RL with Verifiable Multi-level Process Rewards
selected_evidence.text: Abstract: Enhancing the agentic capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) to tackle complex software engineering (SWE) and general terminal-usage problems is a pressing challenge. Current state-of-the-art LLMs often go through large-scale agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL). However, they mostly rely on high-level outcome rewards, with minimal consideration of low-level toolcall and mid-level workflow-stage rewards, which makes the training less effective. To overcome this limitation, we propose **Lean4AgenticRL**, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first framework that grounds multi-level process rewards in the unified Lean4 formalization schema for open-ended agentic RL. **Lean4AgenticRL** first builds a *problem-specific workflow* system that balances the agent's own capability and controllability during execution, laying the foundation for further verification. Subsequently, our workflow formalization and multi-level reward annotation methods enable agent behavior verification within a general harness system. It provides multi-level rewards to support more effective agentic RL with the workflow-stage-normalized GRPO algorithm. Using **Lean4AgenticRL**, we train **LAR-9B/27B**, a family of models with enhanced agentic capability. Extensive experiments indicate that our model outperforms the leading model of similar size. **LAR-27B** achieves **77.3%** on TerminalBench-2.1. On average, our models outperform the base model by **9.89%** and surpass the second-best model of comparable size we know by **5.07%**. These results indicate the potential of integrating formal methods in enhancing open-ended agentic RL.

selected_evidence.title: Structured Authority Injection: Persistent Human Control for LLM Agents via Typed MCP Overrides
selected_evidence.text: Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly used as autonomous orchestrators in distributed and multi-agent systems, yet a control gap remains: no protocol-level mechanism allows human operators to inject binding directives that persist across planning cycles. Free-text overrides suffer from ambiguous interpretation due to lack of schema validation and from authority erosion as operator instructions lose influence within accumulating context. We propose Structured Authority Injection (SAI), a protocol that addresses these issues by routing operator corrections through typed, schema-validated Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool calls and maintaining a ranked authority context prepended to each LLM prompt. SAI defines three override classes (Constraint, Priority, and Strategy) with distinct persistence semantics and an explicit precedence order enforced via a directed authority channel inaccessible to the planning process. The method requires no model fine-tuning or access to model weights and applies to instruction-tuned LLMs supporting MCP tool use. Evaluation across nine LLMs and eight scenarios targeting agent failure modes shows reduced ambiguous directive interpretation and mitigated authority decay across planning iterations, with lower prompt overhead in the strongest models (up to 38% depending on model and scenario), though benefit varies substantially across models. SAI provides a general design pattern for agent systems requiring explicit and persistent human control.

selected_evidence.title: Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution
selected_evidence.text: Abstract: Harness evolution automatically optimizes the prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration code around a fixed-weight model, offering a way to improve agentic systems without updating model weights. The agent harness is iteratively optimized to achieve higher performance on the search set. But how much of this gain reflects benchmark-specific overfitting or additional inference-time compute, and how much may generalize beyond the search set? In this work, we introduce Harness-Delta Attribution (HDA), an evaluation protocol that dissects an evolution gain into artifact-driven overfitting, gains explained by test-time scaling, and the remainder, which gives an upper bound on residual generalizable improvement. We apply HDA to 11 executor models and three harness-evolution frameworks across math, coding, creativity, and agentic tasks. In 21 of these settings that show statistically significant search-set gains, we find that a large share of the improvement is explained by overfitting or test-time scaling. Specifically, among these 21 settings, overfitting and test-time scaling account for 54% and 14% of the gain on average; their combined share exceeds 50% in 14 settings. The residual and held-out transfer vary substantially across tasks, models, and frameworks. Importantly, search-set gains often fail to transfer to held-out tasks, and provide limited evidence that they will persist under practical distribution shifts. Moreover, validation-based signals are insufficient to prevent overfitting. These results motivate attribution-aware evaluation in future harness evolution research.
